title: Chapter 57
content:
"The reattachment surgery appears to have been a success, President Kang."

"And Lee Ja-kyeong?"

"His flight touched down in Korea three hours ago."

Il-hyun glanced down at his platinum wristwatch. Since I told him to come straight to the house, he should be making an appearance soon. It was hard to imagine the boy would walk in guns blazing while an ally was being held hostage, but having taken two bullets from those very hands, Il-hyun wasn't about to drop his guard. He had doubled the armed security around the estate's perimeter, fortifying the grounds for every contingency.

Through the streaming window, the downpour raged with violent intensity.

Without warning, the driver, Sung-min, slammed the brakes to the floor.

Tires shrieked against the slick asphalt as the sedan lurched violently forward. Park Tae-soo whipped his head around from the front passenger seat. "Are you unharmed, President Kang?"

"My apologies, sir! A motorcycle cut right across our nose!"

Frowning at the jolt, Il-hyun straightened his posture, arching a single dark brow. He followed Tae-soo's line of sight through the windshield.

Stationed dead-center across the narrow mountain road in the pounding rain was a black motorcycle.

Sung-min continued to stammer apologies, but the words washed over Il-hyun without registering. Sensing a lethal threat, Tae-soo reached inside his suit jacket, fingertips locking onto the grip of his sidearm.

The rider swung a leg off the bike and reached up, pulling off his full-face helmet.

The heavy sheets of rain blurred the silhouette, but the face was unmistakable: Lee Ja-kyeong.

A low, incredulous laugh broke from Il-hyun’s throat.

The moment Tae-soo reached for the door handle with his weapon drawn, Il-hyun raised a single hand, halting him in his tracks. Leaning his forearm against the leather seatback, Il-hyun watched the scene unfold through the glass with the languid detachment of a man settling into a private cinema.

Standing in the deluge, Ja-kyeong racked the slide of a heavy 12-gauge shotgun, leveling the wide bore straight at their windshield.

Tae-soo’s expression hardened into stone. Il-hyun, on the other hand, broke into a wide, radiant grin.

"Tae-soo."

"Yes, President Kang."

"Isn't he fucking gorgeous?"

Tae-soo glanced back, looking as if he must have misheard the question. The corners of Il-hyun's lips pulled higher, curving into a thoroughly unhinged smirk.

"Looking like that... how the hell am I supposed to keep my sanity?"

Ordering both men to stay put, Il-hyun pushed his door open, stepped onto the wet asphalt, and popped a large black umbrella overhead. Heavy raindrops drummed a furious, deafening cadence against the taut fabric.

Barely thirty feet away, Ja-kyeong stood rooted to the pavement, keeping the shotgun trained dead-center on Il-hyun's chest without flinching an inch.

Fuck. After spending the past twenty-four hours wanting to tear him to pieces, the second he's in front of me, everything goes right out the window.

Il-hyun closed the distance with steady, unhurried strides. Cold rainwater soaked the cuffs of his trousers and ruined his bespoke leather shoes, but he couldn't care less.

When he reached bare feet from the muzzle, every detail of Ja-kyeong’s face resolved into sharp focus.

His skin was kissed by a golden tan, his dark eyes burning with the fierce, feral defiance of a wounded stray, and his drenched frame holding a heavy combat shotgun in the rain was so breathtakingly striking it was practically obscene.

With the wide bore hovering inches from his chest, Il-hyun came to a halt.

"Long time no see."

Ja-kyeong didn't waver, keeping the steel locked on target.

"Still determined not to let me hear that voice, I see."

Il-hyun chuckled, taking another casual step forward until the cold steel barrel pressed firmly against his left breast pocket.

Ja-kyeong tilted his chin up, his dark eyes smoldering with venom. "Where is Wang Ryun?"

Il-hyun reached out, gently pushing the barrel aside with two fingers as he moved to close the gap. Ja-kyeong refused the inch, snapping the muzzle upward until the cold rim was wedged firmly beneath Il-hyun's jawline—a clear declaration that he would blow the man's head clean off his shoulders if he pushed his luck.

Their gazes tangled in the rain.

Standing in the flesh, the lethal malice that had radiated from Il-hyun over the video call had softened into an amused, almost gentle indulgence. Even with a chambered shotgun jammed beneath his chin, the man didn't blink; if anything, he looked as pleased as a guest receiving a bouquet of fresh flowers.

"Your brother is perfectly intact," Il-hyun drawled. "I even had my surgical team sew his finger back on. Though whether the nerve takes remains to be seen."

"..."

"If you'd like, I can connect you right now."

When Ja-kyeong gave no response, Il-hyun dialed a number with his free hand.

The screen illuminated with an active video feed, revealing Wang Ryun sitting upright in a sterile hospital bed, his right hand swathed in thick medical gauze. Compared to the bloody wreck from yesterday's call, his condition was remarkably stable.

Seeing the connection, Ryun lunged toward the lens with wide, frantic eyes.

[Ja-kyeong?! Did you actually fly here?! Are you alone?! I told you to stay the fuck—]

Click.

Il-hyun severed the call with a casual swipe of his thumb.

Ja-kyeong tore his gaze from the black screen, glaring back up at Il-hyun. The sudden, overwhelming relief that Ryun was breathing took the murderous edge off his posture, his rigid shoulders dropping a fraction of an inch.

Il-hyun smiled warmly. "May I share this umbrella with you now? I really hate seeing you get soaked."

Taking a half-step forward, Il-hyun carefully nudged the shotgun barrel away from his jaw with his palm, bringing Ja-kyeong beneath the canopy. The roar of the falling rain filled the heavy silence between them.

Il-hyun extended an open hand. "It's been a whole year... Surely a handshake isn't too much to ask?"

"Cut the bullshit."

Before Ja-kyeong could step back, Il-hyun’s hand shot out, locking around his wrist.

With a sudden, violent yank, Il-hyun hauled him forward. Off-balance on the slick asphalt, Ja-kyeong tumbled straight into the man's broad chest. As he braced his palms to shove away, powerful arms locked around his spine in a suffocating embrace.

Before Jakyeong could process the contact, a sharp, white-hot sting pierced the side of his neck.

His eyes blew wide.

Il-hyun had drawn a concealed syringe from his inner sleeve, driving the needle deep into the muscle and depressing the plunger in one fluid motion. A heavy, burning ache radiated outward from the injection site.

Ja-kyeong shoved him off with explosive force, ripping the needle from his neck and leveling the shotgun once more.

Il-hyun moved like lightning—knocking the barrel aside, tossing the heavy weapon into the weeds, and clamping a large palm around Ja-kyeong’s throat.

The airway clamped shut. Dark spots exploded across Ja-kyeong's vision. He clawed at the iron grip, but the paralytic was already racing through his bloodstream, turning his limbs to lead.

Dangling the half-emptied syringe before Ja-kyeong's unfocused eyes, Il-hyun offered a gentle, apologetic smile. "My apologies. There's still a bit left."

Whether the suffocating dizziness was from the chemical or the crushing grip on his windpipe was impossible to tell.

The world blurred into gray static. Having emptied the remaining dose, Il-hyun tossed the plastic barrel into the gutter.

Ja-kyeong stumbled, whipping a combat knife from his belt and lashing out in a desperate arc. Il-hyun simply leaned back, letting the edge slice through empty air.

Ja-kyeong tried to reverse his grip for a secondary thrust, but his fingers gave out entirely—the heavy steel blade slipping from his numb palm and clattering against the asphalt.

His eyelids fluttered violently, his chest heaving for air.

Il-hyun strolled forward, casually kicking the fallen knife into the underbrush.

Ja-kyeong’s knees buckled, collapsing onto the wet road. He forced his heavy head up, glaring through the rain with everything he had left. Fucking... monster...

Water poured over his face. He tried to spit out a final curse, but his vocal cords refused to form sound.

Il-hyun dropped into a crouch before him, leaning in until his lips brushed the shell of Ja-kyeong’s ear.

"Welcome home, darling."

The deep baritone felt distant, echoing as if from the bottom of a deep well.

"Just sit tight... I'll have you taxidermied so beautifully."

A high-pitched ringing swallowed the sound of the rain. Ja-kyeong reached a desperate, trembling hand toward the grass where the shotgun lay, but his fingers scraped uselessly against the mud.

His body tipped backward, sinking into absolute, fathomless darkness.

Drenched in arterial blood, Ja-kyeong opened his eyes inside a rotting, dilapidated warehouse.

His skin crawled as he watched beetles and rats scurry across the damp concrete floor. He drew ragged, shallow breaths, scanning the shadows—finding nothing but a row of rusted industrial barrels lining the walls.

He tried to push himself upright, but his legs were lifeless dead weight. He collapsed back onto the floor, forced to drag his body on his elbows toward the exit.

A sickening, metallic scratching noise echoed from the drum directly ahead.

He lifted his gaze.

Long, crimson-lacquered fingernails hooked over the rusted rim, followed slowly by the crown of a head. Catching the glint of a gaudy, cheap rhinestone bracelet around the wrist, Ja-kyeong’s pupils contracted in primal terror.

The face emerging from the barrel belonged to his dead mother.

From the adjacent drum, the man he had once called father hauled himself upward—wearing the exact same sadistic sneer he wore whenever he raised a lead pipe, the face of a monster ready to butcher his son into pieces.

Paralyzed with horror, Ja-kyeong clawed backward across the concrete.

The two corpses spilled over the rims like viscous liquid, crawling toward him on all fours like bloated spiders.

["You think you get to survive alone?! You treacherous little bastard!"]

["We should have crushed your skull the day you were born!"]

["I should have snapped your neck instead of your legs!"]

["Come with us! Drag him down with us!"]

Their venomous shrieks tore through his ears like grinding metal. No... Stay away! Get away from me!

Ja-kyeong frantically scrambled for a weapon. But instead of cold concrete, his palms met a smooth, immaculate surface.

He tilted his head back, his jaw dropping in shock.

Standing above him with a surgical scalpel in hand was Kang Il-hyun, smiling down with the face of a radiant demon.

["I'll have you taxidermied so beautifully."]

Without a beat of hesitation, Il-hyun drove the scalpel straight down toward Ja-kyeong's eye.

Gasp!

Ja-kyeong bolted upright in bed, air tearing into his lungs in desperate, violent heaves.

He stared wildly around the room, wiping the icy cold sweat from his face as the realization settled in: it had been a nightmare.

He took a steadying breath, assessing his surroundings. The space was eerily familiar.

It was an expansive, luxurious suite outfitted with a king bed, an integrated kitchen, a dining table, a plush sectional sofa, and high-end amenities.

He swung his legs over the edge, but his knees buckled the moment his soles touched the floorboards. The chemical sedative was still circulating in his system, leaving his muscles heavy and uncoordinated. Remembering the needle in his neck, he ran a hand along his collar, moving forward on cautious, measured steps.

Stepping into the corridor, he was met by a long, polished hallway lined with heavy reinforced doors.

It was Kang Il-hyun’s private subterranean vault.

He scanned the corridor for guards, but the underground floor was completely deserted.

Instead, high-resolution surveillance domes were mounted at every corner of the ceiling, tracking his movements.

Looking down, he found himself dressed in soft, clean loungewear. But a strange, tender ache pulled at his chest; he peeled the fabric back to find both of his nipples swollen, flushed, and marked with deep, distinct teeth indentations.

His lower half was completely untouched.

Realizing what had happened while he was unconscious, Ja-kyeong ground his molars together in blinding rage.

That psychotic, nipple-obsessed degenerate!

Fuming with fury, he stormed down the hall to the private elevator, slamming his palm against the call button. The panel remained dead. He had stashed the silicone biometric glove in his tactical pack, but that kit was undoubtedly in Kang Il-hyun’s possession by now.

He drove his fist hard against the steel elevator doors—THUD! THUD!—but the heavy plates didn't budge a millimeter.

Pivoting on his heel, he checked the adjacent rooms. The walk-in armory and firing range were completely stripped bare; every single weapon had been cleared out, leaving only empty racks and bare concrete.

The entire subterranean level had been converted into an inescapable, gilded cage.

Ja-kyeong clenched his jaw until it popped, fixing a murderous, venomous glare toward the ceiling.

You sick bastard... What the fuck do you think you're doing with me?
